formal_sdp_certificate.meaning: SDP-feasible P proves local asymptotic stability of the SYSTEM-IDENTIFIED linear approximation of the tracking-error dynamics (fit on real RLBench trajectories above), not a proof about the true nonlinear CoppeliaSim physics. Validity is bounded by r_squared=-1.666 on held-out transitions — treat as unreliable below ~0.5.

summary.note: Empirical closed-loop tracking-error monitoring on a real nonlinear rigid-body simulator (CoppeliaSim via RLBench), plus (if --sysid) a formal SDP certificate for a linear model IDENTIFIED FROM the collected trajectories — see formal_sdp_certificate.meaning and r_squared before trusting it. This complements, not replaces, the exact-linearization SDP certificate in safety.json (that one linearizes a known closed-form toy system; this one fits an approximation to a black-box simulator). Policy is untrained unless loaded via --policy-path (see scripts/rlbench_train_bc.py). mean_dist_to_target_reduction_pct (only for tasks in REACH_COMPATIBLE_TASKS, rlbench_gui_demo.py) is a distance-to-target signal INDEPENDENT of task_success_pct (RLBench's binary proximity-sensor check, a tight threshold) and of mean_terminal_tracking_error_norm (a velocity-tracking safety signal, not task progress) — a policy can show large distance reduction while task_success_pct stays 0%, which means it learned real directional signal without precision enough to trigger success; read both numbers, not just one.
